title: The frames of the app host of Air on its links
description: One line of the corpus of air-apps. A message of one link is the def <Link>Message: AppMessage for the stdio of an app, PageMessage for the WebSocket of the host page, FrameMessage for the postMessage of a frame, IdeMessage for the frames of air-apps on the connection of air-ide. The string ${any} matches any value, and ${<name>} binds a value at its first place and matches it after.

Id.description: The id of a request. The answer carries it verbatim.

Version.description: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without a leading zero, a pre-release or a build part.

Instance.description: The id of one instance of a view, which air-ide gives. It is never used twice in one run of air-ide.

Mirror.description: The key of a mirror of the app, which the app gives, such as the path of a repository. The views that show the same state share one mirror.

AppViewChannel.description: The table channel of the page link that mirrors one mirror of the app. Each page that opens a view of the mirror subscribes to it through x-air-app/viewOpen, and no page subscribes to it by subscribe.

AppLinkChannel.description: The channel of the page link of one process of an app: its notices x-air-app/event, x-air-app/callEvent and x-air-app/progress, in the order of the app. No page subscribes to it, and its number changes with each run of the process, so a page ignores the value.

AppsChannel.description: The held channel of the IDE link with the apps of one project.

Origin.description: Who asked for a call. click: a frame of a view, or a view of the Session View through x-air-ide/appToolCall of the holder. action: an action of the app file or of a notification. agent: the proxy tool air_app of a session.

Reason.description: The kind of an error of the x-air-app vocabulary, in data.reason. A receiver ignores a field that it does not know, and it reads the kind of an error from data.reason only, never from the code. appError is an error that an app answered to a call of the IDE: it keeps the code of the app and its message, cut to its first 1 KiB and the count of its bytes, at most 1056 bytes, and no other field of the app.

stderrTail.description: The last lines of the stderr of a process, at most 20: of the process that exited for serverExited. For notStarted of a holder call, they are the lines of the process that starts now, else of its last exit.

problem.description: The problem of the entry of the app, as its state shows it: for appProblem a problem of the registry or of the scan, which no answer of the user allows, and for notStarted of a holder call the problem of the entry or of its run. Its message holds at most 1 KiB, with the count of its bytes after a cut.

request.description: The id of the consent request of the session for approvalPending and toolApprovalPending, when the apps state holds the request: a key of consentRequests. The banner of the session answers it. A write that sets no request gives no id.

ErrorObject.description: A JSON-RPC error. -32001 badTicket, -32002 serverExited and notStarted, -32003 connectionLost, -32004 tooLarge, -32008 unknownChannel, unknownInstance and unknownApp, -32009 noConsent, agentOrigin, notHolder, modelOnly, approvalPending, denied, toolApprovalPending, toolDenied and appProblem, -32011 tooManyCalls, -32601 unknownMethod and unknownTool, -32602 badResource and otherView, -32603 internal, resourceRead, noViews and viewsTimeout, -32800 cancelled; the other codes are those of JSON-RPC and of air-ide.

ViewOp.description: One change of the state of a mirror by the table rule of air-host: part replaces one part, set puts one entry of a part by its key, remove deletes it.

ViewChanged.description: The one state action of an app view channel: the ops of one change of the app, applied in order.

ViewContext.description: What the view of a frame shows: the IDE gives it, and the page never sets it.

actions.description: The actions of the notification. air-ide keeps their runs, so a click runs one of them. The runs of the actions that it shows hold at most 65536 bytes as JSON text together: it drops an action past them with a warning, as one that it cannot run.

Run.description: As Run of air-app.schema.json: a call of a tool with the origin action, or the open of a view.

CallMeta.description: _meta["x-air-app"] of a tools/call that air-ide sends: the origin and the app; the session block of the view of x-air-ide/appToolCall; the view and the instance of a click of a page; the action of an action, and the view and the instance of a title action.

SessionBlock.description: The base of the view of an x-air-ide/appToolCall, which the views channel of the IDE gives: the view, its revision, the verdict, the surface with the tail after it, and the data model. status is null while the revision has no verdict. A new view has the revision 0, no surface and no tail, and the form state of the call as its data model.

visibility.description: Who may call the tool. model: an agent through air_app, with agent.tools model and its consent. app: a frame of a view (origin click) and an action of the app file or of a notification (origin action). Without it, both.

capabilities.description: air-ide offers x-air-app to an app of the user. A project entry is a plain MCP server, so its initialize offers no experimental capability.

AppInitializeResult.description: A project entry is a plain MCP server whatever it answers. Its link reads no x-air-app of this result, and it lists the tools of the app. An app of the user without experimental["x-air-app"] of the major of air-ide is a plain MCP server too. It serves no view and no tool. An error of tools/list refuses a project entry, and an app of the user that answers with capabilities.tools.

count.description: The count of the badge, from 1 to the largest Int of the JVM, or null, which clears the badge.

params.description: A progress has a fraction, a text, or both. A text without a fraction is a progress without a percent. Neither a fraction nor a text clears it.

reason.description: sessionClosed: the app no longer serves the mirror. An app cannot tell a gone repository from a closed session, so version 1 has no other reason.

AppMessage.description: One message of the app link: MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 over the stdio of the app, one object per line.

ticket.description: At least 32 characters of base64url, once: the ticket of the fragment of the address of the host document, or of window.airAppHost.connect.

ViewOpenResult.description: The subscription of the page to the channel of its mirror with its snapshot, or, for a viewOpen with the params of the view that the connection holds, held: true and the channel of that subscription without a snapshot.

reason.description: closed: air-ide closed the channel for another cause. serverExited: the process of the app exited. sessionClosed: the app ended the mirror (x-air-app/viewEnded). A receiver reads an unknown reason as closed.

PageMessage.description: One message of the page link: one JSON-RPC 2.0 object in one text frame of the WebSocket. Every params has channel, as on the connection of air-ide.

FrameInitializeResult.description: hostContext["x-air-app"] is present when the frame offered the extension and the host serves it.

FrameSubscribeResult.description: The subscription with its state, or, for a subscribe of the view that the frame holds, held: true and that subscription without a state.

FrameMessage.description: One message of the frame link: MCP Apps JSON-RPC 2.0 by postMessage between the frame of a view and the host page.

AppEntry.description: One app of the apps channel. A project entry of genui-apps.json has no views, no actions and no instances.

description.description: The description of a project entry, which the agents read. A text over 1 KiB keeps its first 1 KiB and names its length. A text of an app in a log entry or a problem has the same cut. Only when the entry has one.

consent.description: The consent of the command. commandText, envText and coversText are command, env and covers as each banner shows them. Each code point of the general categories Cc, Cf, Cn, Co, Cs, Zl, Zp and Zs but U+0020 is \u{<hex>}, by shown-text.ranges. A text quotes each argument and each value of a variable as ParametersListUtil.escape of the IDE does. A U+0020 after a U+0020 is \u{20}. The three texts hold at most 64 KiB together, and an entry over it has the problem tooLarge, an empty commandText and no fingerprint.

env.description: The variables that the command adds to the environment of the IDE, by name. The banner shows each one as name=value, so a variable such as NODE_OPTIONS that loads code is in sight. Only when the command has one.

covers.description: The paths of covers of a project entry, as genui-apps.json names them, which the banner shows and the fingerprint pins. Only when the entry has one.

commandText.description: The executable and each argument, quoted and joined by one space.

envText.description: Each variable as NAME=value by name, the value quoted, joined by one space. Only when the command has one.

coversText.description: Each path of covers, quoted and joined by one space. Only when the entry has one.

state.description: starting: a first start or a restart of the user, until the process is ready. restarting: from an exit until the process of the backoff restart is ready. failed: the fourth exit in a row, or a refused process.

generation.description: Grows with each restart of the process: a new generation reloads the frame with a new ticket.

connected.description: True while a WebSocket of a host page holds the instance by its ticket. When it turns false while the place stays, the IDE gives the loaded page of the instance a new ticket, unless it loads the page again itself.

CallId.description: The id of an x-air-ide/appToolCall, which x-air-ide/appToolCancel names: a UUID of the IDE, at most 64 ASCII letters, digits and dashes. A call whose callId is in flight gets badParams.

RequestId.description: The id of a consent request, r<n>. One counter of the host of air-ide gives n, so an id is unique in the host.

ConsentRequest.description: A consent request of a session: a holder call that the consent refused. A session has at most one for each target, the entry or the entry and a destructive tool. It names no field of its entry, and the banner reads consent and source of the entry. It lives while its entry keeps the command key, the covers and the source of its start, and while the entry has no problem. An answer of its target ends it, and so does the removal of the app.

owner.description: The session of the call, by the keys of LocalSessionIdentity.

reason.description: entry: the consent of the command, and for a project entry the agent consent of its answer. destructiveTool: the tool consent of tool.

tool.description: The destructive tool of the reason destructiveTool.

consentRequests.description: The consent requests of the sessions by their ids, the oldest first, at most 64. A new one over the bound removes the oldest. The part is absent until the first request of the channel, and appConsentRequestsChanged replaces it whole.

oneOf.description: The answer of the user to the consent banner. It names the command, the variables and the covers that the banner showed: another of them in the entry refuses it with the reason stale before any write, and an answer without them gets badParams. Then an entry without a fingerprint gives the reason of its problem, or noCommand, but a Deny: a Deny of a command whose code no scan read holds by its command key, and air-ide reads no code for it. Last, a request that is gone, or that names another app or the reason destructiveTool, gives stale. An answer ends each consent request of the entry of the app.

command.description: The command line that the banner showed, consent.command of the entry. Another command line of the entry refuses the answer with the reason stale before any write.

env.description: The variables that the banner showed, consent.env of the entry, or {} for none. Other variables refuse the answer with stale.

covers.description: The covers that the banner showed, consent.covers of the entry, or [] for none. Other covers refuse the answer with stale.

agent.description: Whether the answer of a project entry also allows the agents to call it: for the process of Allow Once, or in the record of Always Allow. An app of the user gets badParams.

request.description: The consent request of a session that the banner answers. An answer with it that allows starts the stopped entry.

oneOf.description: The answer of the user to the consent request of a destructive tool, with the command, the variables and the covers that the banner showed, as appConsent names them, and checked in its order. The request must name the app, the reason destructiveTool and the tool, else stale, so an answer for one tool never allows another. allowOnce covers the next agent call of the tool. alwaysAllow joins tools of the record of the fingerprint, and without a record it holds for the process. deny holds while the channel is open. The result of the echo is {changed}.
The agent consent of an app of the user, in the memory of the channel. A project entry gets badParams: its answer names the agent.

The life of a place. The result of the echo is {changed}: whether the shown state of the instance flipped, an instance starting hidden, or for a close whether the instance left the channel. The app hears each report.
An action of the app file. instance names the instance whose place shows the action, such as a title action of a tool window; the call then names its view and its instance.

A click on the action at the index action of the notification that x-air-ide/appNotify numbered notification. air-ide runs the run that it kept of that action, the open of a view or the call of a tool with the origin action, never a run of the IDE. It keeps the runs of the last 32 notifications of the app while the consent covers the fingerprint that it covered then, also across a restart of the process. A number that it does not keep is refused with unknownNotification, an index past the actions with unknownAction, a tool that tools/list of the app does not name for the app, or one of the prefix air_, with unknownTool, and the call of a tool also with noConsent and notStarted.

AppsAction.description: A state action of the apps channel by the table rule: one app entry set or removed by its id, or the part consentRequests replaced whole.

AppViewTicketResult.description: The answer of x-air-ide/appViewTicket. The IDE loads <pageUrl>#ticket=<ticket> in a new browser of the instance, or gives the ticket to the loaded page of the instance by window.airAppHost.connect(ticket) in its main frame. The page opens its WebSocket on the origin of pageUrl.

ticket.description: At least 32 characters of base64url, once.

pageUrl.description: The host document of the page entry of air-ide, http://127.0.0.1:<port>/, the same for each ticket of one run.

Session.description: The session of a holder call, by the keys of the session of a view of the views channel of air-ide.

AppsListResult.description: The answer of x-air-ide/appsList, one message of the IDE. The apps come in the order of their ids. Their tools and instructions hold at most 12 MiB, by the encoded bytes. An app over the rest gets the problem tooLarge and no tools. The descriptions, the problems, the refused entries and the file errors hold at most 1 MiB. Over that budget, a problem keeps its reasons with the message: the message is over the budget of the answer. It then has no tail, a description drops, and a refused entry counts into refusedMore.

description.description: The description of a project entry, cut to 1 KiB.

instructions.description: The instructions of the answer of the app to initialize, cut to 64 KiB. Only for a ready app that gave them.

tools.description: The tools that the model sees, of each page of tools/list of the ready run. The input schema and ui of _meta stay as the app wrote them. A tool without an input schema gets the empty object schema. An app with a problem has none.

problem.description: The data of the error that an agent call of the app gets now, such as agentOrigin or noConsent. notStarted has the stderr tail and the problem of the entry. tooLarge: the tools of the app are over the budget of the answer.

refused.description: The refused entries of the project registry files, in the order of their names. A file keeps its first 64 refused entries by name.

name.description: The name of the entry, cut to 1 KiB.

reason.description: invalidId: the name is no id. remoteServer: the entry names url. tooManyApps: the entry comes after the first 64 apps of its file. invalidEntry: the entry or a field of it is wrong.

message.description: A sentence of the refusal, cut to 1 KiB.

refusedMore.description: The count of the refused entries that the answer does not name: those past the first 64 of each file, and those over the budget. It can count an entry of the committed file whose name a local app takes. Only when there are some.

errors.description: Each project registry file that air-apps cannot read or parse. The file keeps the apps of its last good content.

message.description: Why the file cannot be read or its bytes do not parse, cut to 1 KiB.

AppToolCallResult.description: The answer of x-air-ide/appToolCall: the CallToolResult of the app, and the UI kind of the tool. ui is null for an error result and for a tool without a UI resource, a2ui for ui://air/a2ui, and resource for a resource of the app with its text, which air-apps reads once for each run. A result and a text over one message of the IDE give -32004 tooLarge. A failed read or one with no text gives -32603 resourceRead.

userApps.description: Whether the channel holds the apps of the user of ~/.air/apps. The IDE opens the apps channel of its sessions with false. That channel reads and watches no file of ~/.air/apps, so it holds the project entries only.

environment.description: The base environment of each process of the channel, in place of the environment of the IDE process. The IDE gives the shell environment of the user. Each process gets the variables of its entry, one PATH and PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX over it. The launch drops each PATH of the base, in any case. It also drops each variable by which a program loads or finds code, when its value has a place mark. A place mark is a part . or .. of a path, a ~ at the start of a word, or a place of the process. A mark after a leading short switch or in quotes counts too, as in -I./lib or "./x.js". The PATH of the process is that of the entry, else of the base, else of the IDE. It loses each empty or relative directory, each place of the process and each directory in the project. The check reads the text and the real path of each directory. On Unix it also compares the device and the inode of each ancestor with the project. A PATH with no directory left starts no process, since an empty PATH finds a program in the project. A NUL, an empty name or a name with = gets badParams.

params.description: A command of the apps channel: the request handler of the IDE reads one file of a frame of an app, ui://<app>/<path>, and gets the ReadResourceResult of the app as it wrote it. The channel answers when the app answers, so a read holds no worker of the host while the app reads. While the link of the app is not ready, a read waits at most 30 s. It waits for the run whose start goes on, or for the next run of the backoff. It starts no app. A run that ends before its link is ready gives -32002 notStarted with the stderr tail of now. So do a stopped app and the end of the wait. A read that would wait past the cap of the parked calls of the channel gets -32011 tooManyCalls.

notificationId.description: The number of a notification with an action, by which the IDE runs an action of it, x-air-ide/appNotificationRun. air-ide sends only the actions that it can run, and a notification without one has no number.

name.description: A tool of the IDE: air_copy, air_open_file, air_show_diff, air_show_commit or air_navigate. The badge, the progress and a notification are requests of the app, x-air-app/setBadge, setProgress and notify, and no host tool.

params.description: A command of the apps channel: a call of an agent through the proxy tool air_app, or a click of a view of the Session View, which only the holder sends. A call whose callId is in flight gets badParams. Before the call reaches the app, a worker compares each mark of the run with its path now. The run has the mark of each path that its start read. The run of a project entry also has the mark of each path of an argument. Each project registry file has a mark too. A change waits for one scan. A channel holds at most 64 such calls, and one more gets -32011 tooManyCalls. A failed scan gives -32603 internal, and so does a wait of 30 s for a check or a scan. A call of a stopped project entry with the consent starts it. The call waits for one run: the run that it starts, the run whose start goes on, or the next run of the backoff. The call reaches a run only after a check of the marks that starts while the run is ready. A run that ends first, a failed app and a wait of 30 s give -32002 notStarted with the stderr tail of now. At 30 s the start goes on. Before the start, an entry with a problem of the registry or of the scan gets -32009 appProblem with the problem. A Deny gives -32009 denied. A command that the consent does not cover, or an agent call of a project entry whose answer does not name the agent, gives -32009 approvalPending with the consent request of the session and the entry. At the ready link, a tool that tools/list lacks gets -32601 unknownTool. A click of a tool that the app does not see gets -32009 modelOnly, and an agent call of a tool that the model does not see -32009 agentOrigin. An agent call of a destructive tool needs the tool consent: a Deny gives -32009 toolDenied, and no answer -32009 toolApprovalPending with the consent request of the tool. A tool is destructive unless readOnlyHint is true or destructiveHint is false. A click never asks. A UI resource of the tool that is not ui://air/a2ui and whose host is not the app gets -32602 badResource. Last, the reader of the views gives the session block of the view: else its error, such as -32602 otherView, or -32603 noViews, or -32603 viewsTimeout after 10 s. The answer is AppToolCallResult.

session.description: The session of the call, which owns each consent request that the call sets.

view.description: The view of the call in the views channel of the IDE: the view of the app, or a new id.

formState.description: The form state of the call, the data model of a new view.

params.description: A command of the apps channel: the apps of the channel for the proxy tool air_app, or the one app of app. The list checks the marks of each run, and it starts each stopped project entry with the consent, as an agent call does. Its answer is AppsListResult. An app that is no entry and no refused entry of the channel gets -32008 unknownApp.

app.description: The one app of the list: an id, or the name of a refused entry.

params.description: A root notification of the holder: it cancels its x-air-ide/appToolCall callId in the apps channel apps. The call gets -32800 cancelled at once, and a call that reached the app gets notifications/cancelled there once. A parked call never reaches the app. A cancel of another connection, of an unknown call or of an answered call changes nothing.

IdeMessage.description: One message of the IDE link: the frames of air-apps on the connection of air-ide, in its vocabulary x-air-ide.

LinkFrame.description: One message on one link, from one end. A runner of one end sends the messages of the other end and checks its own.

conn.description: The connection of the line when its link has more than one at a time: a WebSocket of the link page by the order of its handshake, and a connection of the link ide by the order of its initialize, from 1. Without it, the line is on the last one of its link that opened.

raw.description: A line or a text frame that is no JSON message, as sent.

binary.description: A binary frame of a WebSocket, its bytes in base64.

Step.description: An event of the world that a runner makes happen or expects. A runner skips a step that its end cannot see. httpRequest sends one HTTP request without an upgrade and expects its status, the headers by their lowercase names and the exact body. pageLoad is the load of the host document by the IDE and the address of the page after it. pageShow, pageTheme and pageTicket are the calls window.airAppHost.show({frame, theme}), setTheme(theme) and connect(ticket) of the IDE in the main frame of a loaded page. A runner of air-ide skips the four page steps.

frame.description: The frame of the view that pageShow mounts: the resource of the view on the origin of its app.

theme.description: The theme of the IDE that pageShow and pageTheme give the page, as the IDE captures it: dark, and the values of its colors.

StateCheck.description: The mirror of a channel or a subscription after the lines before it, by the table rule.
